label: EdgeSwitch 5 XP
description: EdgeSwitch 5 XP (ES-5XP) - five gigabit RJ45 data ports, each sourcing configurable 24 V passive PoE at 11.5 W, plus a separate 10/100 management port that carries no PoE. The small PoE switch in the EdgeSwitch XP line, on an included 24 V / 2.5 A adapter.
notes:
Vendor figures from Ubiquiti's EdgeSwitch XP datasheet (https://dl.ui.com/datasheets/edgemax/EdgeSwitch_XP_DS.pdf, HTTP 200, application/pdf, 3,915,117 B, 7 pp, text layer, read 2026-11-21) and the tech-spec page (https://techspecs.ui.com/uisp/wired/es-5xp, HTTP 200, 574,944 B, rendered table, same day). p.5, the ES-5XP page, prints "Networking Interfaces: Management Port (1) 10/100 Ethernet Port, Data Ports (5) 10/100/1000 Ethernet Ports", "PoE Out Voltage Range 22-24VDC", "Max. PoE Wattage Per Data Port 11.5 W", "PoE Method Passive", "PoE Configurable Per Port: Management Port N/A, Data Ports Off/24V" and "Power Input 24VDC, 2.5A Power Adapter (Included)"; the tech-spec page prints the same rows as "(5) 10/100/1000 Ethernet ports", "(1) 10/100 Ethernet port", "24V DC, 2.5A power adapter (Included)", "Max. power consumption 60W", "PoE Out voltage range 22-24VDC", "Max. PoE wattage per port 11.5W", "PoE method Passive" and "PoE configurable per port: Management port: N/A / Data ports: Off/24V".

**What this entry got wrong until 2026-11-21.** The census and the passive classification were already right, but the watts were not modelled: all five data ports carried the bare `poeOut: true` bit, which `poeDraw()` bills as **1 W** and the faceplate prints as no figure, and there was no `poe` block, so `pseDraw()` had nothing to sum against and `show power inline` reported the budget as not modelled. Measured before the change: five 11.5 W PowerBeam ACs on eth0-eth4 were all accepted and `poeDraw()` answered **5 W for 57.5 W of load**. The five ports now declare 11.5 W in the passive class.

**The management port was a phantom 802.3af PSE.** On a `poe-pse` device, `media.js` infers a 15.4 W class-0 PSE for any copper port with no declared figure, so `mgmt` was counted as a sixth power port on a five-port PoE switch - and 802.3af is a negotiated 48 V standard this box does not speak. p.5's "Management Port N/A" is the vendor saying it carries no PoE, so `mgmt` now carries `"poeOut": false`, the same fix PR #2433 applied to the ES-16XP's two management sockets.

**Passive, not 802.3af/at.** 22-24 V DC fixed output, configured per port Off/24V: a standard 802.3af/at PD will not negotiate on any of the five ports, which is why the ports are classed `passive` and why the spec advertises the datasheet's `passive-poe` fact. 11.5 W is the published per-port maximum at 24 V - there is no 48 V mode on the 5XP (the 8XP and 16XP are the dual-voltage members).

poe.note: 60 W is the datasheet's own figure for this model, quoted not derived: p.5 "Power Input 24VDC, 2.5A Power Adapter (Included)" and "Max. Power Consumption 60 W", and 24 V x 2.5 A is 60 W, so the row is the included adapter's ceiling. Ubiquiti prints no row labelled "PoE budget" for the ES-5XP and, unlike its EdgeRouter pages (which say "Max. power consumption 16 W (excluding PoE output)"), does not say whether the box's own draw sits inside the 60 W. It is therefore recorded as an input envelope, the same reading devices/ubiquiti/es-16xp.json takes of that chassis's "300 watts of power": five data ports at the published 11.5 W each total 57.5 W, which fits the adapter only if the box draws 2.5 W or less, and that margin is the reason the number is visible here rather than hidden. The tech-spec page prints the same table ("24V DC, 2.5A power adapter (Included)", "Max. power consumption 60W") and no total either. A lab that fits its own supply inside the 24 V input can declare its own figure.
